title: StreamingResponse: Async Generator Chunks and Server-Sent Events (SSE)

progressiveExplaining.eli5: Instead of waiting for an AI model to write a 10-page essay and sending it all at once, `StreamingResponse` sends each word down the wire the instant it is generated, streaming text smoothly onto the screen like a typewriter.
progressiveExplaining.junior: `StreamingResponse(async_generator())` streams data chunk-by-chunk to the client using HTTP `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`. For Server-Sent Events (SSE), set `media_type='text/event-stream'` and yield strings formatted as `data: <content>\n\n`. It allows streaming large files, audio, and live LLM token completions without buffering the full response in server memory.
progressiveExplaining.senior: Architecturally, `StreamingResponse` maps Python asynchronous generators directly to the ASGI `http.response.body` chunk protocol. The event loop yields control after every `yield` expression, flushing bytes down the open TCP connection. It prevents server memory exhaustion when streaming multi-gigabyte files or handling thousands of concurrent real-time AI token streams.
progressiveExplaining.underTheHood: In `starlette.responses.StreamingResponse`, `__call__` sends `{'type': 'http.response.start', 'status': self.status_code, 'headers': ...}`. It then loops `async for chunk in self.content_iterator: await send({'type': 'http.response.body', 'body': chunk, 'more_body': True})`. When the iterator finishes, it sends `more_body: False` to terminate the HTTP stream.

legacyOrBad.label: Buffered Response (High Latency)
legacyOrBad.snippet: full_text = await generate_all(); return {'text': full_text} // ❌ User waits 10s for first word

fullFile.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI
import asyncio

app = FastAPI()

# ❌ OLD: Buffering the entire generation delays TTFB by 5-10 seconds.
@app.get('/chat')
async def chat():
  result = ''
  for i in range(5):
    await asyncio.sleep(1)
    result += f' Token_{i}'
  return {'response': result} # ❌ Client sees nothing until all tokens finish

fullFile.code:
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
import asyncio

app = FastAPI()

async def token_generator():
  for i in range(10):
    await asyncio.sleep(0.3) # Simulates token generation
    # SSE protocol requires 'data: ...\n\n' format:
    yield f'data: Token {i}\n\n'

# ✅ NEW: Real-time token streaming with chunked transfer encoding
@app.get('/chat/stream')
async def chat_stream():
  return StreamingResponse(
    token_generator(),
    media_type='text/event-stream',
    headers={'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'Connection': 'keep-alive'}
  )

interviewGotchas.question: What happens if a client disconnects (closes the browser tab) while a `StreamingResponse` is in the middle of yielding?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Interviewers test your knowledge of client disconnect handling in streaming ASGI endpoints.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: When the client disconnects, the next attempt to `send()` over the ASGI connection raises a `ClientDisconnected` exception (or the iterator detects cancellation). To prevent wasting backend resources (like OpenAI tokens or database bandwidth), check `await request.is_disconnected()` inside your generator loop, or catch `asyncio.CancelledError`.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: If you do not check `request.is_disconnected()`, your generator will continue executing compute and consuming resources until the loop completes.

interviewGotchas.question: Can `StreamingResponse` take a synchronous generator function?
interviewGotchas.contextIntro: Checks precision regarding synchronous vs asynchronous generators in streaming.
interviewGotchas.detailedAnswer: Yes, `StreamingResponse` can accept a synchronous generator (`def gen(): yield ...`), but Starlette runs it inside an iterator loop that can block the event loop if the generator executes synchronous I/O. Always use an **asynchronous generator (`async def gen(): yield ...`)** for non-blocking I/O streaming.
interviewGotchas.trapWarning: Using a synchronous generator that calls `time.sleep()` will block the entire FastAPI event loop during stream generation.
